title: mut.channel_hobbs_fidenza_flow_curves
mutation_directive: Tyler Hobbs — Fidenza structured flow curves — Fidenza (Art Blocks Curated, 2021). VISUAL SIGNATURE: Thick painterly curves following an underlying flow field, but constrained: curves never overlap, and each maintains a confident varying thickness. Reads like pressure-loaded brushwork. Palette: muted earth tones (Luxe), sometimes vivid (Vibrant). Curves of different scales pack the canvas like river deltas. TECHNICAL HOOKS for three.js / GLSL: 2D flow-field but lifted to 3D as a height-painted plane. Generate flow vectors via simplex noise on a 2D grid; integrate streamlines starting from random seeds; for each streamline, sweep a thick varying-thickness ribbon (TubeGeometry on the streamline, with radius modulated). Critical move: collision-detect against existing streamlines so they pack rather than overlap (a quadtree). Render with a flat painterly shader (no specular). Slowly rotate the plane in 3D so streamlines look sculptural. WHY DIVERSE: Pool has flow-field-style ink ribbons but they tangle/overlap freely. Hobbs's specific contribution is the NON-OVERLAPPING constraint that produces packing — visually a totally different result (Voronoi-like, calm) than free flow. Distinct enough to count. Stay faithful to the visual signature; pick whatever three.js primitives are needed (Lines2 / InstancedMesh / SphereGeometry / custom ShaderMaterial) — but the FORM should read as if this artist made it. REF: https://www.tylerxhobbs.com/
